newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia opens first international sea aviation show.
newsitem.headline: Russia opens first international sea aviation show.

text.p: Russia is displaying 150 sea-going aircraft, including new civil and military planes, at its first international show of such craft, which opened on Tuesday at the southern resort of Gelendzik.
Zinovy Pak, Russian Minister of Defence Industry, said at the opening ceremony that the show should become "a fresh impulse for the development of sea aviation in Russia".
"It (sea-going aviation) has excellent potential for civilian use," he said.
More than 300 Russian and international design bureaux and plane makers displayed their production at the one-week show.
Russia is demonstrating a light Be-103 sea plane, a Be-12P-200 fire service plane and rescue A-40 "Albatros" aircraft there for the first time.
Russian military aircraft manufactures are showing new and upgraded carrier-based fighters and helicopters.

A spokesman for the Moscow Aviation Production Union (MAPO), which unites the MiG and Kamov design bureaux and several aviation plants, said the upgraded MiG-29K fighter would go on display after tests on the Russian Admiral Kuznetsov carrier.
The Moscow-based Kamov design bureau is demonstrating its military Ka-50 sea helicopter, rescue Ka-27PS and research KA-32SI helicopters.
